summary: Audited paper/es-threequarter-note.tex: the ONLY ineffective input is Bombieri–Vinogradov (eq. BV, R=26) in the lower bound of Thm supply, over moduli q=4uv ∈ (4X^{1/24}, 4x^{1/3}]; BT, Shiu, lattice sums, moments, void and ledger are effective. BMOR (arXiv:1802.00085, Thm 1.1/1.2 verified: valid only for x ≥ exp(0.03√q log³q) when q>10⁵) cannot replace it — the range is never met for q ≥ X^{1/24}, and pointwise x/(φ(q)log x) bounds summed over q are structurally too weak; Platt–Trudgian is irrelevant here. Assessment (proof sketch): an effective BV off one Landau–Page modulus r1 (Akbary–Hambrook Thm 1.2, explicit c0=48.83, for conductors > (log x)^31; effective zero-free region below) plus BMOR Prop 1.11 (β ≤ 1−40/(√q log²q)) for r1 ≤ (log x)^{1.9}, and dropping the triples with r1 | 4uv (relative mass loss ≪ (log x)^{−1.9+ε}) otherwise, makes c_*, C_* of the 3/4 theorem effective. Premise of `why` fails: N·exp(−c(log N)^{3/4}) → ∞, so no effective/explicit version can ever certify 'no counterexample below X' (data/z52b/pass2/ZF1/Z2418/effectivity.md §5).
not_done: No rewrite of the note; Shiu constant not made explicit (so 'effective', not 'explicit'); log log and m/n notes only grepped, not re-derived; sketch not independently reviewed.
next: Insert an 'effective BV off the exceptional modulus' lemma into the 3/4 note and have it reviewed, changing 'ineffective' to 'effective' in Thm 1.1.

summary: Read SV (Acta Arith. 118 (2005), Thms 1–4, Props 2–3: limit law c_r = Haar measure of lattices with r points in Ω for UNIFORM random congruences mod p, error O(p^{−δ})). Premise: the item's 'linear congruence mod 4cd' is inverted (in all ES divisor forms the modulus is the unknown, p the residue), so I used the exact dictionary p = 4uBC−u−B ⟺ (B,u) solves y ≡ Ax (mod p), A = 4Cu−1, and compared lattice statistics: for uniform A the empirical P(λ1(L_A) ≤ r√p) matches SV/Haar 3r²/π to 3 digits (e.g. 0.0598 vs 0.0597 at r=0.25), but over all 233 996 certificates of the 7254 primes p≡1(4) in [10⁶,1.2·10⁶] P(λ1 ≤ 0.05√p) = 0.349 (Haar 0.0024), rising to 0.463 at 347 primes near 10⁸ (18 946 certificates); log_p max(B,u) is spread over (0.05, 0.6+), not concentrated at 1/2. So ES certificates sit in the cusp (measure ≍ log²p/p of A's), exactly where SV's O(p^{−δ}) law carries no information; no size-law comparison beyond this is meaningful.
evidence: BRAINSTORM/bsA_hecke_cusp_excursions.md (same B3 scale diagnosis for QNR Hecke points)
not_done: No affine (inhomogeneous ASL2) variant and no Type I analogue; no attempt to condition SV on the sparse residue set {4Cu−1}; no residue-class (mod 840) split since the cusp concentration is generic.

summary: Literature verified (arXiv:1708.02610 abstract, Tao–Teräväinen Duke 2019): odd-order log-averaged Chowla and log density 1/8 of every Liouville sign pattern of length ≤ 3 — statements about log-averages over ALL n, silent on the sparse set N_e=(p+e)/4. Computed R(p) and (λ(N_3),…,λ(N_3+7)) (N_{e+4}=N_e+1) for all 102 327 primes p≡1(4) in [10⁶,4·10⁶]; hard = bottom decile of R/log²p within each class mod 840 (and mod 3360), compared with class-matched controls (stratified χ², 200 within-class permutations). Pattern frequencies over all primes are 1/2^k to ±0.002 (k ≤ 3); hard-vs-control: k=1 χ²=0.05 (p=0.82), k=2 χ²=10.6 (p=0.01), k=3 p=0.03, k=4 p=0.29; the k=2/3 signal is a single shift λ(N_7) (z=3.2 mod 840) that drops to z=2.3 under mod-3360 stratification (Bonferroni over 8 shifts p≈0.18), and within-class corr(λ(N_3), log(R+1)) = −0.0015. The real signal is divisor-theoretic and λ-blind: N_3 prime is enriched among hard primes (11.7% vs 10.0%, z=7.0) while λ(N_3) shows z=−0.24.
not_done: Hardness measured by R(p) (the (★) c=1 Type II line), not by full f_II; no Möbius/μ² patterns; KMT sign-pattern paper not read beyond titles/abstracts (its results are again all-n averages); primes > 4·10⁶ not tested.

summary: Inventoried every ES-side use of Siegel (git grep; table in data/z52b/pass2/ZF1/Z3054/siegel_inventory.md): (i) Pollack IJNT 2014 Thm 1.4 inside CAP_DOWN Cor 2.1 / ASTRA_BRIDGE:282 (L(1,χ_{−4n₀}) ≫ W^{−ε²/640L²}, read in sources/pollack_ijnt2014_generalsplit6.pdf §4), (ii) Bombieri–Vinogradov/Siegel–Walfisz in the 3/4, log log, m/n notes and BOARD2_SLATE Thm 8.5, (iii) INVOLUTION_ES2 uses Siegel's integral-point theorem (not L-functions), (iv) the BM main term needs only upper bounds on L(1,χ_p). Verified Goldfeld–Oesterlé h(D) > (1/55)log|D|∏(1−⌊2√p⌋/(p+1)) (D<0, (D,5077)=1; MSRI Book 49 p. 27): at (i) it is a power n₀^{1/2} too weak (Pollack's comparison would need y ≥ n₀^{640/ε²} instead of n₀^{1/4+ε}), at (ii)–(iv) it is not needed. Positive by-product (Assessment): Tatuzawa (L(1,χ) ≥ (ε/10)q^{−ε} with ≤ 1 exception, verified via arXiv:2508.10844 eq. 1.7) makes CAP_DOWN Cor 2.1 effective outside at most one (n≡1 (8)) resp. two (n≡5 (8)) unknown square classes n₀, and (ii) is removable as in Z2418.

summary: Verified BL §2.1/Lemma 2.3 (S_n ≅ Cayley 4A1 cubic over Q, 9 rational lines; Pic Ũ_n = ℤ) and Derenthal arXiv:math/0604194 Table 7 (4A1: 9 lines, '≥ 2 relations', ref. Heath-Brown math/0210333) — so the torsor is not a hypersurface, closing Pass 1's question. Wrote the Cox ring explicitly from the complete-quadrilateral model (13 generators: 4 ℓ_i, 6 e_ij, 3 diagonals; master relation Σ ℓ_i∏_{j≠i}e_ij = 0 plus 6 diagonal trinomials; t_i = ∏_{j≠i}ℓ_j∏_{ab∌i}e_ab) and sympy-checked σ₃(t) = R·(unit monomial) (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z3139_torsor.py). Specialising the six 'w-face' variables (forced to be divisors of n by t₄ = −n/4) to (1,1,1,1,1,n) reproduces ET's Σ^I_n exactly ((2.2),(2.3),(2.8); (x,y,z) = (abdn,acd,bcd)), and n in the ℓ₁ slot gives ET Type II (4abcd = a+b+nc); ET's dilation is the G_m-torsor of Ũ_n. So ET's parametrisation already is the descent — as ET Remark 2.10 itself states (Props 2.2/2.6 are special cases of Heath-Brown's Cayley torsor x_i = ε y_j y_k y_l z_ij z_ik z_il, quoted in BRAINSTORM/graph_cayley_moves.md §2); new here are only the explicit slot dictionary and the variable count: at fixed n it is 3 equations (degrees 4,3,3) in 7 variables on a 3-fold with polylog point count, no circle-method gain (data/z52b/pass2/ZF1/Z3139/torsor.md).
not_done: No Gröbner/saturation check of the full relation ideal (minimal number of relations not determined); Heath-Brown's Cayley paper read only via abstract; 2-adic/integral model of the torsor over ℤ not worked out beyond the λ = −1/4 scaling.

summary: Premise check: the identity-covered set itself is a union of classes, not a set of multiples; its divisor-closure ℳ(B) (n covered if some d>1, d|n, is covered) is, with B = minimal covered elements (primitive). Computed for n ≤ 10⁷ and 12 menus (Mordell mod 840; (★) congruences n ≡ −u (mod 4uC−1), 4uC−1 ≤ K, K = 3…4095, plus evens): uncovered density at 10⁷ ranges 0.114 (K=3) → 0.0026 (K=127) → 0.000040 (K=4095), Mordell 0.00206, while S_B = Σ_{b∈B, b≤10⁷} 1/(b log b) only moves 1.036 → 1.213 → 1.215 (Mordell 1.572; all ≤ Lichtman's 1.6366): Mordell and K=127 have nearly equal uncovered density (0.00206 vs 0.00265) but S_B 1.572 vs 1.213, so S_B does not track the uncovered density — it is set by the smallest uncovered integers (3 alone contributes 0.303). The uncovered set is dominated by uncovered primes (Mordell: 20 513 of 20 602; K=4095: 384 of 398) and decays like the prime count in uncovered classes (Mordell 0.00273 → 0.00206 from 10⁵ to 10⁷ vs (log ratio)^{31/32} = 0.72 predicted), so ℳ(B) has density 1 for every finite menu and sets-of-multiples theory adds nothing beyond counting primes in the uncovered classes.
not_done: Lichtman (arXiv:2202.02384) read at abstract level only (verified: f(A)=Σ1/(a log a) over primitive A is maximised by the primes), used only as a sanity bound; no Type I menus (b=1 line) or growing menus; no Hall/Besicovitch non-density examples (irrelevant: every finite menu leaves a prime-dominated, density-0 uncovered set).
